transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I just can't stand how I look anymore, especially my face. My skin is covered in these horrible, ugly scars and defects, and I feel like it completely ruins my entire appearance.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about these flaws even when other people say they are minor or not noticeable, or is your main fear that people will judge or embarrass you in social situations?

I definitely spend almost all my time obsessing over these flaws, even though everyone tells me they can barely see anything. I constantly ask my family for reassurance, but even when they tell me I look fine, I just can't stop worrying about how ugly my skin and face look. It's really the flaws themselves that consume me, rather than just a general fear of social situations.
Do you find yourself doing things like checking mirrors, comparing your appearance to other people, picking at your skin, or seeking reassurance over and over because of these concerns?

Yes, I do all of those things constantly and it's completely exhausting. I spend hours staring in the mirror, comparing my face to everyone I see, and picking at my skin to try and 'fix' the flaws. I'm also always begging my family to tell me if I look okay, but the relief never lasts.
How much are these appearance worries affecting your daily life, like work, school, relationships, or leaving the house?

I'm not quite sure how much it impacts my daily life overall, and I haven't really thought about it in that way. All I know is that it just makes me feel incredibly stressed and overwhelmed all the time.
Besides worries about your appearance, do you also have other unwanted thoughts or rituals, like fears of contamination, checking, counting, or needing things to feel just right?
No, I don't experience any of those other things like contamination fears or counting rituals. My anxiety and thoughts are strictly focused on my physical appearance and how my face looks.
Do you think these defects in your face really look obvious to other people, or do you think there’s a chance your mind may be exaggerating them?

They are absolutely real and incredibly obvious to anyone who looks at me, so my mind definitely isn't exaggerating them. It's so anxiety-inducing because I know people must be staring at these awful flaws and judging me. There is no way they can't see them when they are right there on my face.
If a dermatologist or several trusted people told you there was no significant defect, would you be able to consider they might be right, or would you be certain they were wrong?

I would be certain they were wrong or just trying to be polite to make me feel better. The flaws on my face and skin feel completely real and obvious to me, which is why I can't accept their reassurance. It's the reason I feel the need to keep seeking out dermatologists and cosmetic procedures to finally fix what I see.
Apart from your appearance, do you have any other fixed beliefs that others say are not true, or is this belief only about your face and skin?

No, I don't have any other beliefs like that. My worries are entirely focused on my face and skin, especially my scars, acne, and how asymmetrical everything looks. There isn't anything else unrelated that I'm obsessed with or that others find unusual.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance that others report are minimal or not noticeable, along with repetitive appearance-related behaviors including mirror checking, comparing, skin picking, and reassurance seeking. The concern is specifically appearance-focused rather than a broader delusional theme, and there are no other non-appearance delusions reported. Although insight is absent/delusional, this presentation is most consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder rather than Delusional Disorder.
